newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Thai insurance firms seen boosting industry.
newsitem.headline: New Thai insurance firms seen boosting industry.

text.p: Thailand's recent move to grant more non-life and life insurance licences will help increase competition and improve efficency in the local insurance industry, a senior government official said on Wednesday.
"The increasing number of insurance companies will stimulate competition," Piphat Intarasupht, director general of Insurance Deparment, Commerce Ministry, told an industry seminar.
"Competition will urge current insurers to improve more in-depth performance in terms of capital, human resources, equipment and management," he said.
The Thai cabinet on Tuesday approved the licensing of a total of 28 new life and non-life insurance companies.
Of the total, 12 would be for life insurance companies and 16 would be for non-life insurance firms.
The capital requirement for new life insurance companies would be 500 million baht ($19.2 million) and for non-life insurance firms it would be 300 million baht, he said.
"New entrants will strengthen insurance business. The high required registered capital of the newcomers will force business owners to carefully conduct their business," he said.
